claim: Traditional clinical prediction models focus on parameters of the individual patient.
source: Traditional clinical prediction models focus on parameters of the individual patient.

These include age, blood in stool, vomiting, breastfeeding status, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), an indicator of nutritional status.

source: Overall, using the AUC as a discrimination metric, the integrative models (AUC: 0.837 (0.806–0.869)) outperformed the traditional model (AUC: 0.809 (0.776–0.842)).

claim: The best performing models were ones in which either the seasonal sine and cosine curves, or the prior patient pre-test component alone was added to the presenting patient information with AUC's of 0.830 and 0.839 (with 80% training data), respectively.
